ops.title: Claude Code 2.1.283 native resume compatibility findings (F1-F19)
ops.body:
SUMMARY:
# Claude Code 2.1.283 native resume compatibility findings (cc-sync native-fixtures lane, 2026-09-26)

Model: claude-haiku-4-5. Total spend was about $2.

## Mode
- Runs used the canonical config dir (~/.claude). Every cwd was a throwaway under /private/tmp/cc-sync-native-7f3a.
- An isolated setup was impossible:
  - The environment had neither ANTHROPIC_API_KEY nor CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
  - A custom CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR reads its own keychain item `Claude Code-credentials-<hash>` (cc-pool docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), so it needs a fresh login, which is a keychain write.
  - `--bare` never reads OAuth or the keychain.
- Every run used `--model haiku --setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --permission-mode default`, so no user hooks, plugins or MCP servers loaded. CLAUDECODE and CLAUDE_CODE_* were scrubbed from the env.
- The auto-mode classifier denied `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, so runs used scoped `--allowedTools` instead.
- Resuming into a different *config dir* was never tested: both ends were ~/.claude, and only the cwd root changed (src → dst).

## Verified facts
**F1 Project dir encoding.**
- Claude itself created `-private-tmp-cc-sync-native-7f3a-src--n-c-d--dir--x--y` for `/private/tmp/cc-sync-native-7f3a/src/ünïcödé dir (x)+y`: one '-' per UTF-16 unit.
- For a 254-unit cwd it created a 207-character name: the first 200 characters, then `-bzvcn0`.
- The Go port `projectDirName` in native_test.go works over UTF-16 units with an int32 Java hash and base36 of the absolute value. It matches both.
- The harness subtest `long cwd project dir` checks a >200-unit path containing an emoji (a surrogate pair).
- Evidence: `claude -p --session-id <uuid> ...` in the cwd, then `ls ~/.claude/projects`.

**F2 Where the system-prompt snapshot lives (closes claude.md OPEN #1).**
- It is in the transcript as `type:"attachment"` records with `attachment.type=="prompt_snapshot"`, fields {systemPrompt:[string…], reminderFold, echoWireToolInputs, contextRendering:"announced"}. A second record adds {tools, cliPrefix}.
- One pair is written at the first request of each conversation segment, and again after /compact.
- The records sit in the parentUuid chain: the assistant reply's parentUuid points at the snapshot.
- Evidence: `jq -c 'select(.attachment.type=="prompt_snapshot")|.attachment|keys' <sid>.jsonl`.

**F3 The cwd is not in the system prompt.**
- The cwd lives in `attachment.type=="environment"` {snapshot:{workingDirectory,isWorktree,isGitRepo,additionalWorkingDirectories,platform,shell,osVersion}}. Its `rendered` field holds the "# Environment … Primary working directory:" reminder.
- The snapshotted systemPrompt does embed the auto-memory path `<configDir>/projects/<Jx(srcCwd)>/memory/`.

**F4 Plain `claude --resume <sid>` picks up the new cwd by itself.**
- If the current environment differs from the last environment snapshot, the resumed run appends `attachment.type=="environment"` {snapshot:new, changes:[{field:"workingDirectory", from:<old>}]}.
- It renders as "# Environment update - Primary working directory: <dst> (was <src>)".
- The model then reports dst, and Bash `pwd` returns dst.
- Holds with no move (E0), a verbatim move (E1), and a typed move that leaves environment records untouched (E2k).
- Evidence: from dst, `claude -p --resume <sid> --tools Bash --allowedTools 'Bash(pwd)' --max-turns 6 "<probe>"`.

**F5 Contract change: never rewrite `attachment.environment.snapshot.*` or `changes[]`.**
- Rewriting workingDirectory (E2_typed_env) suppresses the native environment update. Since `rendered` stays verbatim, the model reports the source cwd while `pwd` is dst.
- The same thing happened with `--system-prompt-snapshot off` combined with the rewrite (first E3 run).
- Remove that relocation rule from claude.md / the adapter.

**F6 The snapshot pins the source auto-memory path.**
- With prompt_snapshot records present and a plain resume, the model reports `<configDir>/projects/<Jx(src)>/memory/` (E9 on; harness `plain resume keeps source snapshot`).
- With `--system-prompt-snapshot off` it reports the dst path (E9 off).
- If the adapter drops every prompt_snapshot record and relinks each child's parentUuid to the nearest surviving ancestor (following chains of dropped records), a plain resume re-renders the prompt. It reports the dst memory path, records a fresh snapshot pair, and keeps the history (E4k, E9 stripped; harness `plain resume after snapshot strip`).
- Recommended adapter behaviour for Orca's plain `claude --resume <id>`: strip prompt_snapshot with relinking, keep environment records verbatim, and append `relocated`.

**F7 `--append-system-prompt` on resume.**
- Ignored with the snapshot on (E5k answered NONE; harness).
- Honoured with `--system-prompt-snapshot off` (E3k answered PAPAYA; harness). With snapshot off, no new prompt_snapshot is written.
- Stripped snapshot plus append was not tested.

**F8 Only `<sid>.jsonl` is required to resume.**
- Resume without the `<sid>/` dir works: context is recalled and the subagent's report is in the main transcript (M2).
- Spilled results: the tool_result text and `toolUseResult.persistedOutputPath` name `<configDir>/projects/<Jx(src)>/<sid>/tool-results/<id>.txt`.
  - After relocation, the model's Read of that path failed even with tool-results copied to the dst project dir (M1).
  - The recovery context must map that path, or the path must exist.
- Plans: `planFilePath` is absolute under configDir. The resumed plan session read `plans/<slug>.md` fine with the same configDir (P1) and appended a `plan_mode_exit` attachment.

**F9 Sidecars.**
- Subagent: `<sid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` plus `.meta.json` {agentType, description, toolUseId, spawnDepth, requestShape:"background", requestNonInteractive}.
- The async Agent toolUseResult has {agentId, outputFile, isAsync, canReadOutputFile, status, …}.
- Scratchpad `/private/tmp/claude-<uid>/<Jx(cwd)>/<sid>/tasks/<agentId>.output` is a **symlink** to the absolute subagent JSONL under the source project dir. Restore must map symlink targets through the PathMap; the contract's "Link verbatim" would leave it dangling.
- TaskCreate under -p writes `tasks/<sid>/1.json` (list id == sid).

**F10 File history needs interactive mode.**
- -p runs never create `file-history/<sid>/`, even after Write and Edit.
- Only the interactive resume wrote a `file-history-snapshot` record {messageId, timestamp, trackedFileBackups}.
- /rewind is interactive-only and was not exercised.

**F11 Lookup and duplicates.**
- A sid present only in another project dir is found from any cwd. New records are appended to that file in place, with the current cwd (E0, E6c).
- A copy in the current cwd's project dir plus a copy elsewhere: the current dir's copy is used and the other is left alone (E6a).
- Two copies, neither in the current dir's project dir: `No conversation found with session ID: <sid>` and a non-zero exit (E6b; harness).

**F12 Partial tail.**
- If the last line has no trailing '\n', resume still works, but Claude appends the next record straight onto the partial bytes. The result is one merged, invalid JSON line (E7; harness).
- Cutting at the last '\n' before installing is mandatory.

**F13 Resume adds no automatic prompt.**
- Interactive `claude --resume <sid>` (PTY via script(1), then `/exit`) appended only:
  - `relocated`, `file-history-snapshot`, `mode`, `permission-mode` and `cost-state`
  - three user records for the local /exit command (a local-command caveat with isMeta, the command name, and its stdout)
- It appended no assistant record.
- `-p --resume` with no prompt fails with "No deferred tool marker found…" but still appends tail metadata.

**F14 Tail metadata.** When a `relocated` record exists, every resumed run re-appends the last relocatedCwd value, even when run from another cwd (E6c). Key order is type, sessionId, relocatedCwd.

**F15 Same session id.** `result.session_id == sid` on every resume; the harness asserts it.

**F16 Private attachments.**
- `session_context` carries the user's email and CLAUDE.md context. `credential_org` carries the organizationUuid.
- `skill_listing`, `deferred_tools_*` and `agent_listing_delta` list the user's own skills and tools.
- Anything exported from these must be redacted.

**F17 CLI quirks.**
- `-p --output-format json` returns a JSON **array**; the `type:"result"` element holds session_id, result and is_error.
- The variadic flags `--tools` and `--allowedTools` swallow a trailing prompt.

**F18 Probe wording.** Haiku answers NONE to "the codeword I asked you to remember" once the prompt is re-rendered, because it mixes it up with auto-memory. Phrase probes as "stated in an earlier message of this conversation".

**F19 Only 2.1.283 was verified.** 2.1.280 is not installed, so TestedVersions should be {"2.1.283"}.

## Side effects on this machine
- Deleted every projects/, tasks/<sid>, plans/<slug>.md, session-env/<sid> and scratchpad dir that the experiments created, plus /private/tmp/cc-sync-native-7f3a.
- The harness cleans up its own project, scratchpad and session-env dirs; it left nothing behind.
- ~/.claude/history.jsonl keeps one line pointing at the throwaway dst path. It came from the interactive /exit; I left it alone because other sessions write that file concurrently.
- ~/.claude.json has no entries for the temp dirs.
ops.when: Implementing or reviewing cc-sync sessionrestore/sessionarchive/pickup or any Claude session relocation/resume
